newsitem.title: UK: Barratt up after analyst briefings.
newsitem.headline: Barratt up after analyst briefings.

text.p: Barratt Developments Plc led UK house building shares higher on Wednesday after positive comments from the company at a series of analyst briefings and after recent signs of strength in the housing market.
Barratt shares were up 12-1/2p at 288-1/2 by 1245 GMT after earlier rising as high as 290p -- their highest for at least five years.
Other housebuilding stocks also rose with Wimpey Plc up 6-1/2p at 133p, Redrow Group up 3p at 165p and Berkeley Group up 3p at 652-1/2.
Analysts said Barratt had been briefing analysts on its progress, reiterating the message of its recent AGM that the company was progressing well.
"It's one thing to be aware of a situation but for a major player to tell you everything is going according to plan is more reassuring," one analyst said.
But he said the stock may struggle to push higher from current levels.
"After this rise, one should say that Barratt has risen as far as it is going to and one should start lookng at other housing shares to move higher on the back of this," the analyst said.
Barratt shares have shown a general uptrend since January 1996 as the combination of house price rises and low interest rates have boosted housing shares.
Halifax building society, Britain's biggest mortgage lender, said recently house prices rose 8.4 percent last year and by 14.9 percent in greater London.
